descriptors.definition: The cost of property, plant, and equipment acquired under deferred payment terms is recorded at its cash price equivalent at the recognition date. The difference between the total payments and this cash price equivalent is recognized as interest expense over the credit period.
inclusion: Present value calculations of future installments using implicit interest rates
Recognition of interest expense over the credit period
exclusion: Nominal total payment amounts as initial asset cost
Immediate expensing of deferred payment financing differences
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard cash purchases by requiring present value discounting and interest separation

descriptors.definition: Entities must choose either the cost model or the revaluation model as an accounting policy and apply it consistently to an entire class of property, plant, and equipment. These alternative bases govern the subsequent carrying value of assets after initial recognition.
inclusion: Selection of uniform accounting policies across asset classes
Subsequent measurement using cost or fair value frameworks
exclusion: Applying mixed measurement models within the same asset class
Applying policies selectively to individual assets rather than classes
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from initial recognition rules by focusing on ongoing asset valuation and adjustments

descriptors.concept_name: Alternative Bases Available For Measurement After Recognition
descriptors.definition: Entities must select either the cost model or the revaluation model as an accounting policy for an entire class of property, plant and equipment. This policy choice dictates how asset values are adjusted subsequent to initial recognition.
inclusion: Entity policy choice between cost and revaluation models
Consistent application across asset classes
exclusion: Inconsistent application of models within a single asset category
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from initial recognition by governing ongoing measurement choices

descriptors.definition: Under the cost model, an item of property, plant, and equipment is carried at its historical cost less any accumulated depreciation and accumulated impairment losses. This represents one of the two primary alternative measurement bases after recognition.
inclusion: Deduction of accumulated depreciation from original cost
Deduction of accumulated impairment losses from original cost
exclusion: Upward adjustments to fair value without explicit revaluation model adoption
Reflecting market value fluctuations directly in the carrying amount
nearby_distinctions: Contrasts with the revaluation model by prohibiting upward re-estimations of fair value

descriptors.definition: Under the revaluation model, an asset whose fair value can be measured reliably is carried at a revalued amount, representing its fair value at the date of revaluation less subsequent depreciation and impairment. Revaluations must be performed with sufficient regularity to prevent material divergence from fair value.
inclusion: Carrying assets at fair value minus subsequent depreciation and impairment
Periodic revaluations based on market volatility
exclusion: Applying revaluation selectively to isolated assets without including the whole class
Maintaining unadjusted historical costs when fair values differ materially
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from the cost model through its reliance on periodic fair value adjustments and market references

descriptors.definition: Depreciation is the systematic allocation of an asset's depreciable amount over its useful life, recognized in profit or loss unless included in another asset's carrying amount. Significant components of an item with distinct useful lives or consumption patterns must be depreciated separately.
inclusion: Systematic allocation over useful life
Separate depreciation of significant asset components
Periodic review of residual values and useful lives
exclusion: Depreciating land with unlimited useful life
Omitting depreciation when market values increase
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from impairment as a routine allocation of cost rather than an unexpected loss in recoverable value

descriptors.definition: Items of property, plant, and equipment are evaluated for impairment using specific accounting standards to determine recoverable amounts and recognize losses. Third-party compensation for impaired or lost assets is accounted for as a separate economic event and recognized when receivable.
inclusion: Identification and measurement of impairment losses
Recognition of receivable third-party compensation in profit or loss
exclusion: Netting replacement asset costs directly against compensation proceeds
Deferring compensation recognition beyond the date it becomes receivable
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from depreciation by addressing sudden or structural reductions in recoverable value rather than systematic allocation

descriptors.definition: The carrying amount of an item of property, plant, and equipment must be derecognized upon disposal or when no future economic benefits are expected from its use or disposal. Gains or losses from derecognition are calculated as the difference between net disposal proceeds and the carrying amount, and are recognized in profit or loss.
inclusion: Derecognition upon asset disposal or loss of future economic benefits
Recognition of replacement part carrying amounts with simultaneous derecognition of replaced parts
exclusion: Failing to derecognize replaced components when new parts are capitalized
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from impairment by representing complete removal from the balance sheet due to retirement, sale, or lack of benefits

descriptors.definition: The carrying amount of property, plant, and equipment is derecognized upon disposal or when no further economic benefits are expected. The resulting gain or loss is calculated as the difference between net disposal proceeds and the carrying amount, and is included in profit or loss.
inclusion: Determining disposal date based on control transfer principles
Calculating gain or loss via net proceeds versus carrying amount
exclusion: Treating derecognition gains as operational revenue
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from routine depreciation adjustments by permanently removing the asset base

descriptors.definition: Financial statements must disclose comprehensive details for each class of property, plant, and equipment, including measurement bases, depreciation methods, useful lives, and a complete reconciliation of beginning and ending carrying amounts. Additional disclosures cover title restrictions, pledged assets, and construction commitments.
inclusion: Reconciliation of beginning to ending carrying amounts showing additions, disposals, and depreciation
Disclosures regarding title restrictions and pledged security
exclusion: Omitting reconciliations for non-material asset categories without policy backing
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from primary recognition and measurement rules by focusing on transparency and financial statement disclosures

descriptors.definition: Entities must disclose measurement bases, depreciation methods, useful lives, and reconciliations of beginning and ending balances for each class of property, plant, and equipment. Additional required disclosures encompass title restrictions, security pledges, and contractual acquisition commitments.
inclusion: Disclosure of measurement bases and depreciation rates
Movement reconciliation including additions, disposals, and revaluations
exclusion: Excluding commitments or encumbrances from explanatory notes
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from measurement rules by providing qualitative and quantitative context to financial statement users

descriptors.definition: When property, plant, and equipment are carried at revalued amounts, entities must disclose the revaluation effective date, involvement of independent valuers, comparative cost model carrying amounts, and revaluation surplus movements. Additional recommended disclosures cover idle assets and fully depreciated items still in use.
inclusion: Effective date of revaluation
Comparison against cost model carrying amounts
Revaluation surplus movement disclosures
exclusion: Omitting restrictions on distribution of revaluation surplus balances
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard cost model disclosures by requiring specialized fair value and surplus tracking metrics
